title: First black station WMRY in the French Quarter and its disc jockeys
summary: After WJBW he joins WMRY with Ernie the Whip, Malcolm Brown, Bob Parker and Israel Augustine; an agency first pays him a salary, then the station hires him full time.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: You know, I went ahead of myself, ahead of myself, because we were in radio, and I wanted to keep on that train.
You wanted to get into television?
No, no, no. That's a faster train. Let's go back. Let's go back for a second. So you worked at JBW. No. JBW, no. What was your further first station you went?

Well, after that, now, here comes WMRY, which is now WYLD. That's wild. WMRY started in the French Quarter by the Court of Two Sisters. Ernie Branger, who was Ernie the whip, he was the major black disc jockey down there. Well, Ernie and I had kept a beautiful relationship all of our lives because he knew my children, I knew his children, I knew his wife and so forth. Even his oldest child today still calls me his uncle. Well, anyway, Ernie and I were in high school together. So, Ernie said, why don't you come to work down here with us? Well, now, in the meantime, by working for myself, there was a gentleman by the name of, I'm trying to think of his name, an agency here by the name of Care Incorporated. So, he picked up whatever monies that I was making on my own and started paying me a salary to go to WMRY to work. That meant I didn't have to do any selling. They were gonna get the business for me. So, I said, well, it's all right by me. And that made me big time. And I started making more money. Eventually, the station took a liking to me because they were getting ready to move. Excuse me, we're knocking up the... So, they were getting ready to move. And they wanted me to come to work for them full time. And they made me another higher financial offer. So, I took that and I told Care goodbye, just like that. So, I wrote the contract with them. And I started working full time for WMRY. And those were the very beautiful days because I got more popular. People would come to the studio to see who I was. And remember, that was the first black radio station in the city. And a lot of people hadn't seen Ernie Branger, Ernie the Whip, myself, Malcolm Brown. Myself, Malcolm Plath, Bob Parker, Judge Israel Augustine.
